findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the upstream repair-tool name in the Context section — use the actual subcommand `git-remote-s3 doctor` (verified against the helper's --help/docs) rather than `git-s3 doctor`.
evidence: Plan Context: "Upstream's `git-s3 doctor` repairs it but is **interactive-only** (crashes on EOF) and **discards** a divergent head"

The awslabs helper's console script is `git-remote-s3` and the doctor is invoked as `git-remote-s3 doctor` (not `git-s3 doctor`) — the plan should verify the exact upstream subcommand name against the tool's --help/docs

Because rebar does not shell out to the upstream doctor (it ships its own non-interactive auto-doctor), no rebar-issued command depends on this string — so this is a descriptive-accuracy fix, not a runtime failure risk
findings.finding: The plan's Context names the upstream repair tool as 'git-s3 doctor', but the actual upstream console script / subcommand is 'git-remote-s3 doctor'; this is an unverified subcommand-name reference (UNVERIFIED/near-MISMATCH). It is non-load-bearing because rebar replaces the upstream doctor with its own auto-doctor rather than invoking it, but the discrepancy should be reconciled so the rationale ('interactive-only, discards a head') is attributed to the correct binary.
findings.location: Context / Problem — 'Upstream's `git-s3 doctor` repairs it but is interactive-only'
scenarios: A reader tries to locate/compare the upstream 'git-s3 doctor' and finds no such subcommand
The mismatched name propagates into follow-on docs and confuses operators about which tool is being avoided
findings.suggested_fix: In the Context bullet, replace 'git-s3 doctor' with 'git-remote-s3 doctor' to match the actual upstream console script/subcommand.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify a back-out/safety mechanism for the auto-doctor (e.g. preserve the original per-head bundles until the merged single-bundle clone is verified, then delete) so a failed heal is reversible.
evidence: 'merges all divergent heads under a repo-level repair lock and collapses them to one bundle'
AC-3 asserts full reachability post-heal but states no safety net if the heal fails or corrupts
The destructive comparison to upstream is justified ('discards a divergent head (data loss)') but no reversibility mechanism is stated for the new merge path
findings.finding: The auto-doctor merge-heal replaces remote multi-bundle ref state (collapses N bundles into one merged tip) — a mutation of the ticket store — but the plan specifies no rollback/back-out path if the automated heal itself produces a bad merge or fails partway.
scenarios: Auto-doctor crashes or errors mid-heal after deleting original bundles, leaving the store in a worse state than the recoverable multi-bundle signature
findings.suggested_fix: State that the merge-heal writes the new merged bundle and verifies a fresh clone + full reachability BEFORE deleting the original divergent bundles, so the pre-heal state remains recoverable on failure.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Place the s3:// helper fail-closed guard in the shared store init/mount core seam (not only src/rebar/_commands/init.py) so library-facade and MCP init paths inherit it, or explicitly document that all init ingress funnels through the guarded seam.
evidence: 'wire that guard into src/rebar/_store/push.py and src/rebar/_commands/init.py so s3:// remotes fail closed when the helper is missing/old'
AC-2: 'store init and push fail closed'
rebar ingress paths: CLI commands in src/rebar/_commands/, MCP server (mcp_server.py), library facades (rebar.*)
findings.finding: The fail-closed availability guard (AC-2) is wired into the CLI command src/rebar/_commands/init.py for the init path, but rebar has three ingress paths (CLI, MCP server, library facades) that reach store init/mount. If library-facade mount/init or the MCP server initializes the store without routing through _commands/init.py, the s3:// fail-closed guard is bypassed and those paths can silently proceed against a missing/old helper — the exact multi-bundle-corruption risk AC-2 exists to prevent.
findings.location: Child decomposition -> Preflight enforcement: 'wire that guard into src/rebar/_store/push.py and src/rebar/_commands/init.py'
scenarios: A consumer using the library facade to mount/init a store with an s3:// sync.remote bypasses the _commands/init.py guard and initializes against an absent/old git-remote-s3 helper, risking multi-bundle corruption.
An MCP tool invocation that triggers store init reaches the same init path without the CLI-layer guard, so the fail-closed check does not fire.
findings.suggested_fix: Move the require_s3_helper() init-time gate into the shared init/mount core function that CLI, MCP, and library facades all call, mirroring the push.py placement which already sits in the shared store layer.

findings.checklist_item: State in the Auto-doctor child that the heal holds the git-remote-s3 per-ref (IfNoneMatch) lock across the entire enumerate→merge→publish→prune span (re-enumerating bundles UNDER that lock as a TOCTOU guard, and bailing out non-destructively if the lock cannot be acquired), so the remote read-modify-delete is atomic against a concurrent writer or a second healer — not merely serialized by a local repo-level lock.
evidence: Plan: 'merges all divergent heads under a repo-level repair lock and collapses them to one bundle' — names only a repo-level (local) lock
Plan Out-of-scope: 'the helper already auto-steals a stale lock after TTL' — covers a crash, not a live concurrent writer
Context: the multi-bundle state is created by 'a client without the IfNoneMatch lock' — i.e. a concurrent-writer race, which a local-only lock cannot serialize
The heal is a read-modify-delete across enumerate→merge→publish→prune; without a remote per-ref lock held for that whole span it is a TOCTOU on the remote bundle set
findings.finding: The Auto-doctor (merge-heal) child specifies only a LOCAL 'repo-level repair lock' to serialize the heal, but the heal's read-modify-delete of REMOTE S3 bundles (enumerate all bundle heads → merge → publish new bundle → delete originals) is only atomic against a concurrent push or a second host running the same heal if it also holds the git-remote-s3 per-ref (IfNoneMatch) lock over that whole span. The plan's out-of-scope note ('the helper already auto-steals a stale lock after TTL') addresses only a crashed healer, not a concurrent writer/second-healer that adds a THIRD bundle (or re-races the prune) mid-heal — exactly the multi-writer condition the Context says CREATES the multi-bundle state.
findings.location: Child decomposition → 'Auto-doctor (merge-heal)'; Out of scope (helper lock TTL)
scenarios: Two hosts detect multi-bundle for the same ref and heal concurrently; both enumerate the same original keys, both publish a merged bundle, and each deletes the other's originals — leaving multi-bundle or a lost head
A legacy/old-helper writer pushes a new bundle for the ref between the healer's enumerate and its prune, so the prune leaves a bundle the merge never incorporated
findings.suggested_fix: Amend the 'Auto-doctor (merge-heal)' responsibility to require the healer to acquire the helper's per-ref remote lock first, RE-ENUMERATE the ref's bundles under that lock before merging, and no-op/return cleanly (heal deferred) when the lock is already held — the local write lock alone only serializes threads within one checkout, not cross-host/concurrent-writer bundle races.

findings.checklist_item: Survey existing git-remote-s3 forks/variants (e.g., retain-old-head-until-ancestor behavior, maintained forks with altered locking) for non-destructive multi-bundle healing and justify the bespoke merge-heal auto-doctor against them, not only against upstream's interactive discard-based doctor.
evidence: Plan asserts upstream doctor is 'interactive-only (crashes on EOF)' and 'discards a divergent head (data loss). Not usable', then commits to a bespoke merge-heal without considering other prior art for the same fix.

Retrieved source (bgahagan fork of git-remote-s3): 'An old head is retained until a new head is pushed that includes the old head as an ancestor, at which point the old head is deleted. This prevents any data loss' — a distinct, existing non-destructive strategy for the exact multi-bundle divergence the plan heals.
Retrieved sources show maintained forks (fduplex-git-remote-s3, xorq-labs/git-remote-s3) with locking/behavior additions that the plan does not weigh against building its own healer.
ABSENCE: plan gives no comparison of the merge-heal design to any fork/variant repair behavior — only to the interactive upstream doctor.
findings.finding: The novel merge-heal auto-doctor is justified only against upstream's interactive discard-based doctor; the plan does not survey whether an existing git-remote-s3 fork/variant or configuration already provides non-destructive multi-bundle healing, which is the core anti-reinvention question before building a bespoke merge mechanism.
findings.location: Child decomposition — 'Auto-doctor (merge-heal)'; Context / Problem — 'Upstream's git-s3 doctor ... discards a divergent head'
scenarios: An existing fork already heals multi-bundle non-destructively, making the bespoke merge-heal redundant or reducible to a config/dependency choice.
A fork's retain-until-ancestor approach could be simpler and lower-risk than merging arbitrary divergent heads under a repair lock.
